title: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn ·《一个分裂的世界》— 他们等他赞美自由世界，他在雨里说：你们失去了勇气
title_en: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn · A World Split Apart — They expected praise for the free world; in the rain he said you have lost your courage

questions.question: 索尔仁尼琴 1978 年在哈佛批评西方「法条化的生活」。他的核心论点是什么？
options: 西方的法律太严苛，限制了个人自由，应当大幅削减法规、回归传统道德
西方的法律体系形同虚设，权贵可以随意违法，所以必须加强执法
法律本身就是压迫的工具，西方应当像苏联一样以意识形态取代法律
没有客观法律尺度的社会可怕，但除了法律再无别的尺度的社会同样配不上人：法律上站得住就不再问对不对
questions.explanation: 他说自己在共产政权下活了一辈子，深知没有客观法律尺度的社会可怕；但西方把一切冲突交给条文，只要法律上正确就不再要求自我约束、放弃权利或牺牲，每个人都把自己推到法条的极限。他批评的不是法律太严或太弱，而是法律成了唯一的尺度。
questions.question_en: At Harvard in 1978, Solzhenitsyn criticized the West's "legalistic" way of life. What was his core argument?
options_en: Western law is too strict and curbs individual freedom, so regulations should be slashed and traditional morality restored
Western law is a facade the powerful flout at will, so enforcement must be strengthened
Law itself is an instrument of oppression, so the West should replace it with ideology as the Soviet Union did
A society with no objective legal scale is terrible, but one with no scale except the legal one is also unworthy of man: once something is legally defensible, no one asks whether it's right
questions.explanation_en: He said a lifetime under communism had taught him how terrible a society without objective law is; but the West settles every conflict by the letter, and once legally in the right, no one is asked for self-restraint, renunciation or sacrifice—everyone pushes to the edge of the legal frame. His target isn't law being too strict or too weak but law becoming the only measure.

questions.question: 索尔仁尼琴说西方「没有任何审查制度」，却仍存在某种限制思想的机制。他指的是什么？
options: 时髦与不时髦的思想被挑剔地分开，后者从不被禁止，却几乎进不了期刊、书籍和课堂
政府通过秘密的审查机构暗中删改出版物，只是不对外公开
法律虽然允许言论自由，但诽谤罪的处罚太重，人们因为害怕被起诉而普遍不敢公开发言
大公司直接收购报社，下达统一命令规定什么能报道
questions.explanation: 他说东方的报刊被严格统一，西方没有统一命令，却逐渐显出共同的偏好趋势，合力的效果是同化而不是竞争：不时髦的思想并没有被禁，只是没有讲台。关键在于这里没有任何发号施令的机构，说成秘密审查或统一命令，就把他的观察说回了苏联模式。
questions.question_en: Solzhenitsyn said the West has "no censorship at all," yet still has a mechanism that restricts ideas. What did he mean?
options_en: Fashionable and unfashionable ideas are fastidiously separated; the latter are never banned but have little chance of reaching journals, books or classrooms
The government secretly edits publications through hidden censorship bodies it doesn't acknowledge
Speech is legally free, but libel penalties are so harsh that fear of lawsuits keeps most people from speaking publicly
Big corporations buy newspapers and issue uniform orders on what may be reported
questions.explanation_en: He contrasted the strictly unified Eastern press with a Western press under no common orders that nonetheless drifts toward shared preferences, so the combined effect is assimilation, not competition: unfashionable ideas aren't banned, they just get no platform. The point is that no one issues commands—calling it secret censorship or uniform orders turns his observation back into the Soviet model.

questions.question: 2018 年这篇演讲四十周年时被大量重新引用。按文章的分析，这种引用方式漏掉了什么？
options: 引用者夸大了他对苏联的批评，其实他在演讲中主要是在为苏联体制辩护
引用者忽略了他的地缘政治预言后来全部应验，只把它当成文化评论
引用者误以为他主张推广社会主义，而他实际上推荐的是西方式的议会民主制度
引用者多只取「勇气的衰落」，很少提他同样拒绝把西方推荐为俄国的样板
questions.explanation: 文章说这不是误读，而是节选：重新打捞者引的几乎都是批评西方的那段，很少接着引他拒绝推荐西方模式，也很少提他真正的药方是「自愿的、宁静的自我克制」。说他推荐西方式议会民主恰好相反：他拒绝了西方模式，萨哈罗夫还批评过他对威权的容忍。
questions.question_en: For the speech's 40th anniversary in 2018 it was widely re-quoted. By the article's analysis, what did that way of quoting leave out?
options_en: Quoters exaggerated his criticism of the Soviet Union, when in the speech he was mainly defending the Soviet system
Quoters overlooked that all his geopolitical predictions later came true, treating it as mere cultural commentary
Quoters wrongly assumed he favored spreading socialism, when he actually recommended Western-style parliamentary democracy as a system
Quoters mostly took "the decline in courage" and rarely noted that he also refused to recommend the West as Russia's model
questions.explanation_en: The article calls it excerpting rather than misreading: revivers quoted almost only the critique of the West, seldom the refusal to recommend the Western model, and seldom his actual remedy of "voluntary, inspired self-restraint." Saying he recommended Western parliamentary democracy is the reverse: he rejected the Western model, and Sakharov had criticized his tolerance of authoritarianism.
